status: Post-review exploratory sensitivity analyses; specified before new fits, not preregistered
baseline: Fresh raw ZIP -> enrollment audit -> anchors/features -> explicit next-7-day outcome -> structural 81-pair pool -> all supported pair and three-presentation refits. Reuse published algorithms, no reuse of old features or fitted predictions. This is independent execution, not independent implementation or external replication.
endpoint: Y=1 if no observed event in (anchor+d, anchor+d+7]; observed course span must cover endpoint. This does not validate dropout or completeness of provider logging.
recent: At every source fitting/evaluation role and T1/T2 evaluation, require an observed event in (anchor+d-7, anchor+d]. Source role assignment remains the baseline enrollment-level stratified 60/20/20 split using the new outcome; recent activity then restricts each role. All vocabulary, preprocessing, predictor, calibration and OOF fits are repeated. No change to source-only hyperparameters or support cutoffs.
joint: Use explicit new outcome and the structural 81-pair pool. Globally assign each user to the eligible provider/base-course with earliest observed enrollment event, breaking ties lexically. Retain all presentations of that one base course. Assignment precedes source roles and every fit; uses no labels. This changes the population and does not correct all original-population intervals. Recent-activity restriction is a separate sensitivity, not crossed with assignment.
identity_boundary: T1 excludes every S-presentation user; T2 excludes every S or T1 user, including those not active or used to fit models. Across-course identity audit uses the full original rosters conservatively.
update: Frozen S predictor; historical full-source-calibration Platt versus T1 full Platt, fixed-historical-slope intercept, count-weighted parameter shrinkage. Original nested unstratified budgets 0.1,0.2,0.5,1 and seeds. No T2 label enters fitting or tuning. Matched S/T1 label-count sensitivity also rerun with the published procedure.
support: Published thresholds unchanged: source train minority>=5, validation minority>=2, calibration N>=30 and minority>=10; target/T1/T2 N>=50 and minority>=10. Update budget N>=10 and both classes, no redraw. All structural candidate/day/seed attempts and failure reasons retained.
aggregation: Average seeds within pair or triple, then equal weight to those units. Cluster bootstrap by provider/base-course, 100000 draws, seed 20261012; pointwise intervals. A has a 12-contrast family (2 new sensitivities x 3 days x 2 models); U has separate 6-full-budget and 96-strategy/budget families within each sensitivity. These are approximate multiplicity sensitivities, not exact confirmatory guarantees.
heterogeneity: All base-course mean U and leave-one-base-course-out macro U, all methods and budgets. Report sign shares, range and largest changes; no deletion selected to improve a result.
absolute_performance: T2 event prevalence, raw/historical/full/intercept/shrink Brier, recent-rate null Brier, U and uncertainty, counts. All averages are macro averages, not pooled sample-weighted estimates.
comparability: Also compare baseline and each sensitivity on common supported pair/triple/day/seed/model jobs. Differences remain population-and-refitting sensitivities, not causal effects.
reproduction_checks: Compare raw audit counts, feature tables, endpoint tables, support keys, pair/rollout scores, conservative and matched scores to frozen previous outputs. Record observed numeric deviations, not assumed equality; investigate any discrepancy before reporting success.
limitations: Course-cluster intervals condition on completed fits; no full pipeline bootstrap. Base-course identifiers and timing are inferred from logs. Same-base presentations are not independently sampled. No inference of equivalence from intervals covering zero.
delivery: Aggregate report, tables, plots, protocol and runnable extension source; learner IDs and prediction caches remain private. Manuscript and existing submission package unchanged during experiment stage.
